title: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing against Microsoft 365 tenants
text: A reverse-proxy phishing kit is being used to bypass multi-factor authentication. Victims receive a shared-document notification and are redirected to https://login-m365-verify.example/common/oauth2. The proxy relays the real sign-in flow and steals the session cookie once MFA is completed, allowing the attacker to replay the token. Infrastructure resolved to 203.0.113.45. Within hours, inbox rules were created to hide security alerts. Organisations should monitor impossible-travel sign-ins and token reuse originating from login-m365-verify.example.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Voice phishing targeting help desk staff
text: Callers impersonating employees contacted the IT help desk and requested a password reset and the enrolment of a new MFA device. They used personal details gathered from social networks to answer verification questions. After the reset, the attacker logged in from 203.0.113.150 and searched the mailbox for payment information. The same group later sent follow-up emails from it-helpdesk-support.test asking other staff to approve push notifications. Help desks should enforce call-back verification.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Session token theft linked to M365 phishing kit
text: Incident responders investigating unauthorised mailbox access traced the initial event to a document-sharing email. The victim authenticated on a proxied page served by login-m365-verify.example, which captured the session cookie. A second hostname, sso-m365-verify.example, was registered by the same actor. Both resolved to 203.0.113.45. The intruder downloaded contact lists and sent internal phishing to colleagues. Revoking refresh tokens and resetting credentials stopped the activity.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: QR code phishing in fake parking fines
text: Printed notices placed on car windshields asked drivers to scan a QR code to pay a parking fine. The code opened https://city-parking-pay.example/fine?ref=55A1 on the mobile phone, outside corporate protections. The page requested card data and a mobile banking password. Email variants of the same lure embedded the QR code in a PDF attachment so that secure email gateways could not inspect the link. The domain was hosted on 192.0.2.201 and used a free TLS certificate.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Fake shared-drive notification phishing
text: Users were notified that a colleague had shared a confidential spreadsheet. The button led to a lookalike file-sharing portal at drive-share-files.test, which asked for corporate credentials before displaying the document. Credential submissions were forwarded to 198.51.100.190. The emails came from compromised accounts of partner companies, so the sender reputation was good and the messages bypassed filtering. Security awareness teams should remind staff to open shared documents from the official application only.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Phishing through collaboration chat messages
text: External tenants sent chat messages to employees claiming to be the internal IT team. The messages explained that the mailbox was full and requested the user to re-authenticate via https://teams-it-support.example/mailbox. Because external chat was allowed by default, the messages were delivered without warning banners. The landing page harvested credentials and forwarded them to 203.0.113.201. Restricting external chat federation reduced the exposure.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: AiTM phishing infrastructure expansion
text: The reverse-proxy phishing operation targeting cloud email expanded with three new hostnames: auth-m365-verify.example, login-m365-verify.example and mfa-m365-verify.example. All of them point to 203.0.113.45 or to the neighbouring 203.0.113.46. The phishing emails now impersonate voicemail notifications. Detection should rely on conditional access policies and token binding rather than on domain block lists alone, because new domains are registered every week.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Crypto wallet phishing via fake support portal
text: Users of a cryptocurrency wallet were contacted on social media by fake support agents. They were asked to 'synchronise' their wallet on wallet-sync-support.example, which requested the recovery phrase. Several victims lost funds within minutes. The phishing site was served from 192.0.2.88 and protected by a reverse proxy. The legitimate project never asks users to share their seed phrase.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Bank impersonation phishing targeting SMEs
text: Small businesses received emails pretending to come from their bank and warning about a blocked transfer. The link led to hxxps://secure-bank-validation[.]test/unlock, which reproduced the online banking interface and asked for the activation code sent by SMS. Operators then called the victims to obtain additional codes. Hosting was traced to 198.51.100.211.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Business email compromise following AiTM phishing
text: A manufacturing company suffered a payment fraud after an accountant authenticated on a proxied login page at login-m365-verify.example. The attacker reused the stolen session from 203.0.113.46 and inserted himself in an ongoing conversation with a supplier, changing the bank details of an invoice. The transfer was recovered thanks to a quick reaction by the bank. Phishing awareness and payment verification procedures were reinforced.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Calendar invitation phishing with malicious ICS
text: Attackers abused calendar invitations: the ICS file included a meeting link to https://meeting-join-now.example/j/4471 that requested credentials before joining. The invitation was automatically added to calendars even when the email was quarantined. Some variants also offered a 'meeting plugin' with SHA-256 fe2b8cb806d06f0a38ff9f806a01ffd378844a6fe6b0aca594db7dbb8d858264, but the main objective of the campaign remained credential phishing. The domain was hosted behind 192.0.2.120.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Spearphishing for information against researchers
text: Academic researchers working on energy policy were approached by a fictitious journalist asking for an interview. After building trust over several emails, the actor sent a link to a questionnaire hosted at https://press-interview-forms.test/q/7, which required logging in with a university account. The goal was to collect credentials and information about ongoing projects. The domain press-interview-forms.test was linked to 203.0.113.18, previously used in similar social-engineering operations.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: NightVault ransomware intrusion at a regional hospital
text: The NightVault operators encrypted file servers of a regional hospital after a two-week dwell time. Before encryption, they deleted volume shadow copies with vssadmin and stopped backup services. Around 300 GB of data were exfiltrated to cloud storage, then a ransom note threatened publication on a leak site. The encryptor binary had SHA-256 ab12b8a1a7f51f0b57174e86bf6bc35ea403a35542c95c5dd5941ec371ebb1b1 and appended the extension .nvault to files. Command-and-control traffic was observed to 198.51.100.77.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: NightVault affiliate playbook
text: Analysis of a leaked NightVault affiliate playbook shows a standard double-extortion workflow: initial access is bought from brokers, domain admin rights are obtained, backups are destroyed and the locker is deployed through group policy. The playbook references the negotiation portal nvault7xk2qpl4mzd3r5t6y7u8i9o0p1a2s3d4f5g6h7j8k9l0zxcv.onion and the staging server 198.51.100.77. Affiliates receive 80 percent of the ransom payment, which is requested in cryptocurrency.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Data leak site publishes NightVault victims
text: The NightVault leak site listed eleven new victims this month, including a law firm and two municipalities. Stolen archives are published when the ransom deadline expires. The group uses a file-sharing mirror at nv-files-mirror.example to distribute archives. Negotiators demand payment within seven days and threaten to contact customers of the victim. The encryption component is unchanged since February.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Ransomware deployed after VPN appliance exploitation
text: Operators of the Shardlock ransomware gained access by exploiting an unpatched VPN appliance, then moved laterally with remote desktop and encrypted 400 workstations over a weekend. The exploitation is only the entry point; the report focuses on the encryption and extortion phase. The locker (SHA-256 da81b791df68a686338fc4faf0d2ed3f65a6ff9e3eaad631cde7e9975930f8cf) communicates with 192.0.2.177 to register the victim and retrieve the public key. A ransom of 40 bitcoin was requested.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Education sector ransomware wave
text: Several universities reported encrypted file shares and wiped backups at the start of the summer holidays, when staffing is reduced. The ransom notes referred to a group calling itself Paper Owl and demanded payment to https://paperowl-support.example/chat. Files received the extension .owl. The encryptor hash is dd7edb88eac3391663f095bc5f8e6693a5ff2c50bd3e0891e666bd60c9443d6b. The attacks are attributed to the same affiliate based on identical tooling.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Cloud storage encryption by ransomware actor
text: An actor used compromised cloud access keys to encrypt objects stored in buckets with server-side keys under his control, then deleted the original versions. The ransom note was uploaded as a text object in every bucket and requested contact through bucket-recovery-desk.test. API calls originated from 203.0.113.140. This cloud-native extortion does not require any malware on endpoints.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: NightVault decryptor reliability issues
text: Victims who paid the NightVault ransom reported that the decryptor failed on large databases, leaving files corrupted. Incident responders recommend testing decryptors on copies only. The encryptor sample ab12b8a1a7f51f0b57174e86bf6bc35ea403a35542c95c5dd5941ec371ebb1b1 is still used by most affiliates, and the C2 198.51.100.77 remains active.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Ransomware spread through remote desktop
text: Attackers brute-forced an internet-facing remote desktop server, created a local administrator and spread to the file servers. A locker dubbed Mirelock encrypted 2 TB of documents. The binary MD5 is 0df004b3cd92c15d82357f9a389bcd3b. The note directed victims to http://mirelock-decrypt.test/id. Remote desktop exposure remains a frequent root cause of ransomware incidents in small organisations.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Healthcare ransomware attack disrupts appointments
text: A clinic network cancelled appointments after its scheduling system was encrypted. The attackers wiped backup snapshots and left a note signed by the Cobalt Mantis group. Payment instructions referred to cobaltmantis-pay.example. The encryptor SHA-256 is 82d5c3fb14c11344096a908be6695b37b1c4a885c80d7de0ae1a34f303e6b38d. Patient data theft is under investigation, and authorities have been notified.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Shardlock ransomware leak site analysis
text: The Shardlock group published a leak site listing victims from retail and hospitality. The site mirrors are hosted at 192.0.2.177 and 192.0.2.178. Shardlock demands ransoms proportional to the victim revenue and offers a discount for fast payment. The encryptor da81b791df68a686338fc4faf0d2ed3f65a6ff9e3eaad631cde7e9975930f8cf has not changed.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Paper Owl ransomware hits a city council
text: The Paper Owl group encrypted the servers of a city council, disrupting online services for citizens. The ransom note again pointed to https://paperowl-support.example/chat. The locker hash dd7edb88eac3391663f095bc5f8e6693a5ff2c50bd3e0891e666bd60c9443d6b matches earlier education-sector incidents. The council refused to pay and rebuilt its environment.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Ransomware-as-a-service recruitment post
text: On a criminal forum, the operators of a new ransomware-as-a-service called Ember Fox advertised for affiliates experienced in network intrusion. They offer a Windows and Linux locker, a leak site and a negotiation team. Their panel was hosted at 203.0.113.222. Test samples shared with affiliates include f9fa0e5938bb82d5c0567539a0a86bfcccc92b4804fd328f0d8c08cdc454d79a. Encryption speed is presented as the main selling point.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Quartz remote access trojan capabilities
text: The Quartz RAT gives its operator full control of the infected host: keylogging, webcam capture, file management and a remote shell. Persistence is obtained through a Run registry key named 'OneDriveSync'. The implant beacons every 60 seconds to 192.0.2.150 on port 4444 and falls back to quartz-update.test. The dropper MD5 is 50b96a1b663dcaac5dde54ee83ef7b28. Traffic is encrypted with a static key.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Cryptominer botnet targeting Linux servers
text: A botnet exploits weak SSH passwords to install a cryptocurrency miner on Linux servers. A shell script removes competing miners, adds a cron job and downloads the miner from http://198.51.100.101/xmr.tar. The mining pool proxy is pool-proxy-relay.example. Infected servers show constant high CPU usage. The miner binary SHA-256 is 2837117cca6267e1ad5344abe287a68e9b0009fb74b27e5b0d5cad97af6b9eef.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Banking trojan web injects targeting European banks
text: The Vesper banking trojan injects fake forms into online banking pages to capture one-time codes and initiate fraudulent transfers. Its web-inject configuration is downloaded from vesper-cfg.test and targets twelve European banks. The trojan is installed by a loader (SHA-256 1bc30080a03f5e9c2a244feacaf2f67a905831cbb4e0d2c1b630cda91876aed8). Infected hosts communicate with 198.51.100.150.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Quartz RAT new variant with plugin system
text: A new Quartz variant supports downloadable plugins for password recovery and remote desktop. The main implant still beacons to 192.0.2.150, while plugins are retrieved from http://quartz-update.test/plugins/rdp.bin. The sample hash is 7ce594710cd30a39965336c01e0032cf. Antivirus detection rates remain low because each build is packed differently.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Malicious browser extension stealing sessions
text: A malicious browser extension posing as a PDF converter was installed by thousands of users. It reads cookies of social and banking websites and sends them to https://ext-analytics-hub.example/collect. The extension package hash is 5f08058cfeae1e4f7ca5e283b6d64ba825e038b776d44de560ebcebfebd0f593. Session cookies are then used to hijack accounts without passwords. The extension has been removed from the store, but local installations remain.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: IoT botnet Mirage used for denial-of-service
text: The Mirage botnet infects routers and IP cameras through default credentials. Infected devices receive commands from 198.51.100.66 and launch traffic floods against gaming servers. The bot binary for ARM devices has MD5 a80c5006b274da42623dbded57ed5f2b. The botnet counts approximately 25,000 devices. Operators rent attack capacity on criminal forums.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: DLL side-loading backdoor in signed application
text: A backdoor named Lantern is loaded through DLL side-loading: a legitimate signed executable loads a malicious DLL placed in the same folder. Lantern communicates with lantern-telemetry.invalid over HTTPS and supports file upload and command execution. The DLL MD5 is 45a4be9ec80bcd7687c9e95335815e70. The legitimate executable helps the malware evade application allow-listing.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Android spyware disguised as a messaging app
text: A spyware application distributed outside official stores imitates a secure messaging app. It records calls, reads SMS messages and tracks the location of the device. Data is sent to chat-secure-sync.test. The APK SHA-256 is 14c273f23621d3d0decb46bba45e35c28293e709c9e313ea39cfc6e213736e32. The campaign targets activists and journalists in specific regions.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Cryptominer spreading through exposed container APIs
text: Attackers scan for container management APIs exposed without authentication and start containers running a cryptocurrency miner. The image downloads the miner from 198.51.100.101 and connects to pool-proxy-relay.example. The miner binary SHA-256 2837117cca6267e1ad5344abe287a68e9b0009fb74b27e5b0d5cad97af6b9eef is shared with the SSH botnet described earlier.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Macro-based downloader in Excel documents
text: Excel documents with malicious macros download a backdoor called Tinder Moth. When the user enables content, the macro drops a script that retrieves the payload from http://docs-preview-cdn.test/d/tm.bin. The payload MD5 is 7a498c8edbfb732aee3c2e8a43a4aa16 and it beacons to 192.0.2.210. The backdoor collects system information and waits for commands.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Quartz RAT used by multiple actors
text: The Quartz RAT builder leaked on a forum and is now used by several unrelated actors. Samples share the same code but different C2 servers. One recent build still uses quartz-update.test, while another one connects to 198.51.100.205. Attribution based solely on the malware family is therefore unreliable.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Modular backdoor with encrypted C2
text: A modular backdoor named Silt uses a custom encrypted protocol over HTTPS to reach silt-cdn-edge.example. Modules provide screen capture, credential dumping and proxy capabilities. The core module has SHA-256 8bfff66a440809596400d25809150f2d7dec0f46e8899d5d95601ae3ed974711. The backdoor was found on servers of a telecommunications operator.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Exploitation of Acme VPN gateway authentication bypass
text: A critical authentication bypass in the Acme VPN gateway (CVE-2099-0142) is actively exploited. A crafted request to the management interface returns a valid session without credentials. Attackers then upload a web shell to https://vpn.victim-gw.example/dana-na/auth/shell.cgi. Mass exploitation attempts came from 198.51.100.140. Administrators must apply the vendor patch and check the integrity of the appliance.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: SQL injection in a ticketing platform
text: An SQL injection vulnerability in the search function of a widely used ticketing platform (CVE-2099-0450) lets attackers dump the user database, including password hashes. Attackers automated the exploitation with a public tool and targeted public administrations. Exploitation requests came from 192.0.2.44. A patched version is available and the vendor recommends rotating credentials.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Web shells found on Acme VPN appliances after patching
text: Even after patching CVE-2099-0142, several organisations discovered web shells left on their Acme VPN appliances. The implants survive updates by modifying a system script. Investigators identified the web shell file with MD5 0b30df529275994ec6c2ecc8b2ab5963. Connections to the shells came from 198.51.100.140 and 198.51.100.141. A full factory reset is recommended for compromised devices.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Windows kernel privilege escalation exploited in the wild
text: A local privilege escalation in a Windows kernel driver (CVE-2099-0518) is being exploited to obtain SYSTEM privileges after initial access. The exploit triggers a use-after-free in the driver and overwrites a token. The exploit binary SHA-256 is da1e6749f32bf745cd800382d47ee22ecaf3255a38eb496fe72f2290df0d644b. It has been observed in post-exploitation toolkits used by several intrusion sets. The monthly security update fixes the issue.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Browser zero-day exploited through watering hole
text: A memory corruption vulnerability in a browser rendering engine (CVE-2099-0733) was exploited as a zero-day. A compromised news website in the energy sector served the exploit from https://news-energy-today.example/js/analytics.js. Successful exploitation led to the execution of a first stage with SHA-256 fc8e2c5f3114cb780528297cab460a49b5d2e9a3bcf592f3d7ecdebaaa2e5d62. The browser vendor released an emergency update.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Ticketing platform SQL injection - new attack wave
text: A new wave targeting the ticketing platform SQL injection (CVE-2099-0450) was observed, this time from 192.0.2.44 and 192.0.2.45. The attackers exfiltrated customer support tickets that contained sensitive attachments. Organisations that have not applied the update should consider their instance compromised.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Exploitation of SMB vulnerability for lateral movement
text: An intrusion set exploited an unpatched remote code execution vulnerability in the file sharing service (CVE-2099-0901) to move laterally inside networks after initial access. The exploit tool (MD5 8708a4670bc5cf9d3689140a9ba24cfc) scans the internal subnet and compromises vulnerable servers. External command servers included patch-mgmt-sync.invalid. Network segmentation limited the spread in some environments.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Second vulnerability in Acme VPN gateway
text: A second vulnerability affecting Acme VPN gateways (CVE-2099-0957), a stack overflow in the SAML handler, is now exploited. Attackers chain it with the earlier authentication bypass. Exploitation traffic was seen from 198.51.100.141 and 198.51.100.142. The vendor published mitigation XML files pending a permanent fix.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Exploitation of a collaboration server template injection
text: A server-side template injection in an enterprise wiki (CVE-2099-1004) allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code. Shortly after the advisory, exploitation started from 203.0.113.250. The attackers created administrator accounts and installed a cryptocurrency miner in a few cases, but most activity consisted of reconnaissance. The exploit request targets the endpoint https://wiki.corp-intra.test/template/aui/text-inline.vm.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: IoT camera firmware vulnerability exploited
text: A buffer overflow in the web interface of IP cameras (CVE-2099-1188) is exploited to install a bot. The exploit is sent from 192.0.2.17 as an HTTP request with an overlong parameter. Thousands of cameras remain unpatched because the vendor has discontinued the product line.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Linux privilege escalation exploit published
text: A public exploit for a Linux kernel race condition (CVE-2099-1250) allows local users to gain root privileges. Attackers already present on web servers used it to escalate privileges. The exploit binary SHA-256 is b815e7fd53f2de30483fd0c4cae0ec1dabafb7e14e899f321a6517247f3eb99f. Distribution vendors have released patched kernels.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Exploitation of an unauthenticated API in a monitoring tool
text: An unauthenticated API endpoint in a network monitoring tool (CVE-2099-1402) lets attackers create administrator accounts. Vulnerability scanning for the endpoint started from 198.51.100.170. After exploitation, the attackers retrieved stored device credentials. The vendor fixed the issue and released detection guidance.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).
